name: Lazarus Patient Transport & Triage Scrub
description:
Designed for Lazarus paramedics, triage nurses, and patient transport staff — the people working the threshold between the clinic and the street — these scrubs prioritize durability and biological containment over comfort. The base fabric is a tight-weave synthetic that resists fluid penetration and can be decontaminated with standard spray-down protocols without degrading. They come in Lazarus's institutional teal, with a white caduceus-and-serpent logo on the left chest and a QR-linked ID patch on the right shoulder that feeds staff credentials to hospital intake systems. The cut is deliberately loose to allow full range of motion under emergency conditions.

Augmentation compatibility is a design priority: the scrub has pre-reinforced port-access points at the standard wrist, forearm, and dorsal-neck BCI locations, and the fabric around these panels is elasticized to conform to different chrome profiles without tearing. For geneware-modified staff, the scrubs are available with tail-slot rear panels and furred-lining options at the collar and cuffs to prevent chafing on modified skin. Lazarus triage staff working Tier 1 zones often add personal armor inserts to the torso panels — not officially sanctioned, but Lazarus HR has quietly updated the uniform spec to accommodate it.
cultural_context: Lazarus teal is a complicated color in GLMZ. In Tier 1 and 2, it means someone's coming to help — or it means Lazarus is here to document who survives for billing purposes. Triage staff develop their own relationship with the uniform, often personalizing it in ways that humanize them to patients who've learned to distrust the corporation.
story_hooks: A triage nurse notices her ID patch is logging patient contact data that gets routed to a Lazarus subsidiary she's never heard of, not the hospital system.
A counterfeit Lazarus scrub set is being used by someone providing off-the-books medical care in Tier 1 — and they're better at the job than most of Lazarus's licensed staff.
After a mass-casualty event, a transport worker realizes the QR ID system routed all Tier 1 patients to a Lazarus overflow facility that no longer appears on any public registry.

physical_description.visual_profile: Institutional medical wear with deliberate looseness for emergency mobility. The silhouette reads clinical but tactically considered — a uniform that signals both care and containment. Wearer appears ready for physical exertion and biological hazard.
physical_description.fit: Intentionally relaxed through the torso and sleeves to accommodate full range of motion and layered armor inserts. Tapered at wrists and ankles with reinforced elasticized cuffs. Pre-fitted port-access panels at wrists, forearms, and neck that contour around augmentation without bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Tight-weave synthetic ballistic composite designed for fluid resistance and decontamination durability. Feels smooth and cool to touch, slightly stiff when new. Faintly reflective under certain angles.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, clinical finish with subtle ribbing along reinforcement seams. Port-access panels are slightly raised with elasticized edges. Neck and cuff linings (when geneware-modified version) are soft synthetic fur, contrasting the rigid body fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Institutional Lazarus teal as primary — a blue-green that reads both medical and corporate. Crisp white caduceus-serpent logo on left chest. Right shoulder features a matte-finish QR-patch with biodata encoding. Natural fabric wear creates lighter stress-pattern zones.
physical_description.closures: Full-length magnetic snap front closure with concealed overlap. Elasticized wrist and ankle cuffs with friction-fit adjustment. Reinforced seams throughout — designed to withstand repeated decontamination spray-downs.
distinctive_features: Pre-reinforced port-access panels at wrist, forearm, and dorsal-neck BCI standard locations
Elasticized conforming zones around augmentation ports that stretch to different chrome profiles
QR-linked ID patch on right shoulder — feeds credentials to hospital intake systems on scan
Caduceus-serpent branding in high-visibility white on left chest
Concealed torso panel slots designed for armor inserts (unofficial but accommodated in spec)
Optional tail-slot rear panels and furred collar/cuff linings for geneware-modified staff
Slightly oversized cut allows layering of tactical inserts without visible bulk
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. High durability and technical features signal institutional access. The teal color carries ambiguous status — lifesaving in Tier 1, predatory billing in others.
physical_description.cultural_context: Lazarus triage staff exist in liminal space: neither street medics nor corpo doctors, but the threshold enforcers. Wearing this uniform means you answer calls from both clinics and alleyways. Personal modifications and patches are common — staff humanize the corporate teal with individual markers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Micro-stress patterns from repeated decontamination spray-downs visible around seams. Small reinforcement patches common at high-flex zones. Logos crisp but fabric slightly faded from exposure. Personal patches or insignia often added by wearer over time.

Close detail on reinforced port-access panel conforming around chrome wrist. QR-patch visible on right shoulder glowing faintly. Dark atmospheric lighting with medical green accent lighting.
